candidates.title: AMOs translate their address twice (read walk, then write walk), so one AMO can load from one physical page and store to another, sets PTE.A on a store page fault, and loses PTE.D on its own PTE; a failed SC also sets PTE.D
candidates.component: Interpreter (src/interpret.cpp execute_AMO / execute_SC, with src/translate-virtual-address.hpp), shared by native interpretation, the uarch program, the collectors and every log producer
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md component table: 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program ... | Honest operator'). The same code is the pristine uarch program that the deployment fixes on-chain, so the deviation is part of the state transition function itself, identical on every path.
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp execute_AMO (~line 1358): read_virtual_memory<T, STATE_ACCESS, true>(vaddr) (~1364) and then write_virtual_memory<T>(vaddr, valr) (~1369), each with its own TLB lookup (TLB_READ, then TLB_WRITE set) and, on a miss, its own translate_virtual_address walk (PTE_XWR_R_SHIFT, then PTE_XWR_W_SHIFT). src/interpret.cpp execute_SC (~1314): the failed-SC path calls write_virtual_memory<T, write_mode::skip_write>, whose walk sets PTE.D. src/translate-virtual-address.hpp translate_virtual_address: the A/D update (pte_update_mode::update) happens in each walk once that walk's own permission check passes.
candidates.description: The RISC-V A extension defines an AMO as one memory operation that atomically loads from the address in rs1 and stores the result 'back to the original address'. The privileged spec's translation process (4.3.2) runs once per access, with the access type store/AMO. Step 5 checks permissions for that access type, and only then does step 7 set pte.a, plus pte.d for a store. The emulator instead translates an AMO twice. First the read path (read TLB set, read-type walk) loads the value, then the write path (write TLB set, store-type walk) stores the result. Each path consults a different TLB set and may walk separately. Three manifestations follow, all observed on both native and uarch. (a) Split translation. With a stale read-TLB entry V->P1 and a write-TLB entry V->P2 (the PTE was changed to P2 without sfence.vma and the write TLB was refilled by a store), 'amoadd.d old,1,(V)' returns P1's value (100), leaves P1 unchanged, and writes 101 into P2, overwriting P2's 200 without reading it. That is neither the old-translation result (P1=101) nor the new one (P2=201). The same split can send the store half to a device page (for example HTIF tohost) while the load half came from memory. (b) Spurious A on a faulting AMO. An AMO on a page whose leaf PTE is R=1, W=0, A=0 raises the store/AMO page fault (mcause 15) but leaves pte.a = 1 (PTE 0x...03 -> 0x...43), because the read walk passed its own permission check and updated A before the write walk failed. The spec stops at step 5 with a page fault and no A/D update ('the PTE update must be exact, i.e., not speculative'). The same holds for an X-only page under MXR. (c) Lost D. An AMO on the PTE word that maps its own page (A=0, D=0, W=1) loads the PTE after only A was set (0x...47), the write walk then sets D, and the AMO's store writes back 0x...47, clearing D although the page was just written. A single store-type translation would have set A and D before the access, and the AMO would read and write back 0x...c7. Related site, same class: an SC without a reservation fails (rd=1, no store) but its skip_write walk sets pte.d (0x...47 -> 0x...c7) for a store that is never performed. An R1 hunter noted this one but did not report it.
candidates.trigger: Guest code at S or M level (with MPRV) that uses AMOs or SC under paging: (a) a PTE changed without sfence.vma while the read and write TLB sets hold different translations for the VA; (b) any AMO on a readable but non-writable page whose PTE has A=0 (or an X-only page with MXR=1); (c) an AMO on a self-mapped PTE; and a failed SC on a writable page with D=0. An input can steer a guest it controls into any of these. A correct guest only meets (b), and the failed-SC case, in ordinary operation (Linux user-space AMOs on read-only COW pages, futex AMOs, failed SC loops).
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template. Every guest-writable register and memory assignment is presumed reachable (section 2), and paging, AMOs and SC are ordinary RV64IMAFDC + Sv39 features. The bare-metal probe reaches all four effects within 5,000 mcycles from mcycle 0.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No. The trigger is guest execution in a reproducible machine. It needs no machine-API call, no snapshot, no unreproducible mode and no deployment violation. The exclusion 'Guest software that an input can subvert, as long as R7 and R8 hold' does not apply, because the defect is an R7 deviation of the emulator itself.

2 Role: interpreter and uarch program, 'Honest operator' per the AUDIT.md component table. The uarch program fixed on-chain contains the same code, so every path agrees and no R2/R3 divergence exists.

3 High/Medium cases: the Medium case 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)' fits if one argues as follows. (a) needs a missing sfence.vma between a PTE change and the AMO, which Linux on a single hart does not leave open. (c) needs a self-mapping PTE, which Linux never creates. A spurious A bit or D bit ((b) and the failed SC) only perturbs page aging and writeback heuristics, with no isolation or integrity effect. The manual says nothing about A/D updating or AMO translation (grep of doc/README.md), so the deviation is undocumented. Preferred rating: Medium.

4 Critical (alternative reading): R7 says 'The emulator implements the RISC-V specification ... In these areas, any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths', and lists 'Address translation and memory permissions' and 'Atomics and fences'. All three manifestations fall in those two areas, at reachable states: an AMO not atomic on any single physical location, an A/D update outside the specified translation order, and a lost D bit. Under the literal reading this is a rule violation at a reachable state, so Critical, as earlier R7 deviations in these areas were given a Critical alternative. What decides between the readings: whether R7's area-scoped 'any deviation' overrides the Medium case's 'no correct guest relies on' qualifier.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred) / Critical (literal R7: address translation and atomics are listed areas where 'any deviation' subverts a correct guest)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not make paths disagree. Native, uarch and collectors computed identical root hashes, so no wrong claim or proof follows. The threat runs through R7. A correct guest relies on AMO atomicity and on exact A/D semantics for data integrity: dirty tracking decides writeback, and an AMO must read and write the same location. Manifestation (a) silently corrupts a page the guest never read through the AMO, and (c) hides a modification from dirty tracking. An input that controls user code can reliably produce (b) and the failed-SC case, and so plant spurious A/D bits in kernel-managed PTEs. That subverts kernel page aging and writeback decisions, though it does not obviously break isolation. Even where no guest relies on it, the behavior violates R7 as written.
candidates.evidence: Bare-metal probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALESCAPE/amo.c (built with bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh), driven by /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALESCAPE/amo.lua: lua5.4 amo.lua amo.bin amo.elf. Observed: (a) amo old=0x64 read from P1, after the AMO P1=0x64 (unchanged) and P2=0x65 (was 0xc8); (c) self-PTE AMO old=0x20200847, PTE afterwards 0x20200847 (D clear); (b) AMO on R-only page: mcause=0xf, mtval=0x1000c000, PTE 0x20244803 -> 0x20244843 (A set); failed SC: rd=1, target word unchanged (0), PTE 0x20244c47 -> 0x20244cc7 (D set). The same machine run per mcycle with run_uarch + reset_uarch ends with an identical root hash, so the behavior is consistent across native and uarch. A broader probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r8/GOALESCAPE/vm.c (Sv39/Sv48, stale TLB, MPRV with an M->M trap, SUM/MXR, page-crossing fetch faults, AMO/LR/SC, devices through virtual gigapages, timer interrupts) showed no native/uarch divergence (diff.lua, 109,182 mcycles, checkpoints every 13/61/997 mcycles) and no mismatch between collect_mcycle_root_hashes(period 16) and native run hashes (coll.lua, 6,824 hashes).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua builds amo.c with the harness builder and creates a 64 MiB bare-metal machine from it. It runs to halt and asserts the specified behavior. (a) After the split-TLB AMO, either (P1==101 and P2==200) or (P1==100 and P2==201), and the AMO's rd equals the value of the location that was updated. (b) After the faulting AMO on the R-only page, mcause==15 and the leaf PTE's A bit is still 0. (c) After the AMO on the self-mapped PTE, the PTE has both A and D set. Optionally, after a failed SC (rd==1), the PTE's D bit is still 0. Each assertion fails deterministically today, and the test exits 1. It also checks run_uarch per mcycle against the native root hash, so a fix keeps the paths in agreement.

not_covered: Regenerated Solidity step / EVM harness on the AMO probe: not run. Consistency with the on-chain verifier rests on native == run_uarch root hashes, since the step replays the uarch.
log_step_uarch / verify_step_uarch and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes on the AMO probe's mcycles: not run.

ASan/UBSan build was not run on my probes. Host-memory safety of TLB hot slots, fetch cache, PMA lookup, page walk and device offsets was established by reading (page-aligned ranges, shadow_tlb_verify_slot on every cold-to-hot promotion, find_pma requiring full containment, read_ram_uint64 bound to RAM, receive_cmio_request capped at the tx buffer length). Found sound.
uarch stack depth: only bounded by image size (the uarch image ends near 0x699a10, the stack starts at 0x800000, about 1.4 MiB of headroom). Stack frames were not measured precisely.

Sv57 (compiled out by NO_SATP_MODE_SV57), PLIC sources (none in reproducible machines), VirtIO devices (unreproducible only), soft-float semantics, exhaustive CSR/WARL and exception-priority checks: not covered.
Linux guests: probes were bare-metal only. Whether the Linux kernel or guest tools ever hit the AMO split or self-PTE cases in practice was reasoned, not measured.
Guest tools (libcmt, rollup CLI, rollup-http-server), Dave, the PRT player/bridge and the referee model were not examined in this angle beyond what the goal-escape path needed.

Fetch-cache vs code-TLB coherence across every status path was checked by reading (each TLB_CODE writer returns a status > success or happens at trap/interrupt time) and exercised by the probe. Not exhaustively fuzzed.
